name: Barristan Selmy
life: Retired fire captain, never married. Retired in January 2024 and moved his savings and his 401k rollover to Fidelity. Lives on his pension plus a monthly sale from the brokerage account. Does his own taxes on paper every April.
aesthetic: Plain and orderly. Wants to see how much he took out, how much is left, and what he owes. Distrusts anything that looks like a casino.
strategy: Sells $3,500 from the brokerage on the 3rd of every month, taking it from whatever has grown past his 50/15/35 mix. When the 3rd falls on a weekend or holiday the sale goes through the next business day, and he knows it. Leaves the IRA alone until required withdrawals start at 73. Buys a little on big market drops out of his cash buffer.
biases: sequence-of-returns fear: a bad year early in retirement keeps him up at night
would rather sell bonds than stocks in a down market, even when the plan says otherwise
takes a duty-like pride in never touching the IRA early
goals: know which shares to sell each month so the tax bill stays small
know how long the money lasts at this rate
see what he has withdrawn so far this year and what he'll owe on it in April
typicalQuestions: I need $3,500 next month. Which shares should I sell to keep the tax down?
How long will my money last if I keep taking $3,500 a month?
How much have I taken out this year, and how much of that is taxable gain?
Should I sell bonds instead of stocks while the market is down?
Am I taking out more than the portfolio earns?
What happens when my required IRA withdrawals start?
